solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Real’s reserve in seat, tense and very fidgety (11)

indicatorNotes.very fidgety: fidgety letters cannot keep still, so IN SEAT T V shift into a new order

blocks.note: a sub is a reserve player
IN and SEAT as written, T = tense, V = very; anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A Real Madrid substitute squirms on the bench, desperate to get on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Real' dresses up as the football club, with the reserve on its bench; it is the plain adjective. 'Very' reads as an intensifier but only supplies V to the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the formal sense: having real substance rather than being merely apparent.

entries.clue: Dismissed from field, went off in new direction (6,3)

blocks.note: a baseball sense: a batter with three strikes is out and leaves the field
an idiom for boldly setting off on a fresh course

annotation.surface: A player sent off the pitch storms away somewhere else.
annotation.walkthrough: Both halves read as one story about a sacked player walking off; they are two separate senses of STRUCK OUT.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: one sense from baseball dismissals, one an idiom for setting off boldly on a new path.

entries.clue: Truss wearing dress with sex appeal, helping dispute settlement process (7,11)

blocks.note: to truss is to bind
someone wearing a dress is in it
garb is dress, clothing
IT is old slang for sex appeal
a helping of food is a ration

annotation.surface: A politician named Truss in a sexy frock somehow helps settle an argument.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital T makes 'Truss' look like the former Prime Minister Liz Truss; it is the verb. Five short synonyms line up in clue order.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: an arbitrator decides the quarrel, and both sides are legally bound by the ruling.

entries.clue: Florist’s last cut flower (5)

indicatorNotes.last: last means final, so only the closing letter of 'Florist' is used

blocks.note: last letter of florist
rent is an old past tense of rend: torn, cut

annotation.surface: The florist's final job is trimming a bloom.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'flower' in crosswords is often a river, something that flows; the florist makes you think of blooms. The Trent is a major English river.
annotation.definitionFit: Crossword-only sense: a flower is anything that flows, and this is one of England's longest rivers.

entries.clue: Ornamental accessory of one making out with boss? (11)

blocks.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle, so one who does it is a necker
a chief is a boss

annotation.surface: An office romance: what does the employee who snogs the boss wear?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Making out' sounds like working something out; here it is necking, which suits an accessory worn at the neck.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a square of cloth knotted round the throat for decoration.

entries.clue: Film of popular British runner, say, best in the middle (2,6)

indicatorNotes.in the middle: only the central letters of 'best', those in its middle, are taken

blocks.note: what is in is popular
B = British
a runner is a long narrow rug, one example of a rug
middle two letters of bESt

annotation.surface: A popular British athlete, ranked best, is the subject of a film.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Runner' looks like an athlete; it is the strip of carpet laid along a hallway.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a 2008 black comedy starring Colin Farrell and Brendan Gleeson.

entries.clue: Digested crowns troubled EU dental nurses (12)

indicatorNotes.troubled: troubled letters are stirred up into a new order
indicatorNotes.nurses: to nurse is to hold close, so the rearranged letters hold CAPS

blocks.note: anagram fodder EUDENTAL, rearranged and split EN…ULATED
dental crowns are caps

annotation.surface: A news item about dental nurses unsettled by EU rules on crowns.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Digested' is used in the sense of summarised, a report boiled down. 'Nurses' looks like the job title in the surface; it is the verb that wraps the letters round CAPS.
annotation.definitionFit: Synonym in the sense of summarised: a digest boils material down to its essentials.

entries.clue: Redevelopment of ski resort initially excellent investment (4,7)

indicatorNotes.Redevelopment of: redeveloping something rebuilds it in a new form, so SKI R is rebuilt
indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of 'resort'

blocks.note: SKI as written plus R, the first letter of resort; anagram fodder
capital is an old-fashioned word for excellent

annotation.surface: Rebuilding a ski resort is pitched as a first-rate investment.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole resort seems to be the fodder; only its first letter joins SKI.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: money put into a speculative venture, one kind of investment.

entries.clue: Creating reconstruction of space probes responding to stimulus (10)

indicatorNotes.probes: a probe goes inside something, so EN pushes into REACTING

blocks.note: reacting is responding to a stimulus; split RE…ACTING
an en is a printer's space

annotation.surface: Space probes are rebuilt to test how they respond.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Space probes' reads as spacecraft; 'space' is the printers' en, and 'probes' is the verb. EN is half an em, a unit of type width.
annotation.definitionFit: Paraphrase: historical societies act out old battles to recreate them, performing the event again.

entries.clue: Mustang maybe driving up southern coastline (5)

indicatorNotes.driving up southern: the S for southern is driven up to the top of the down entry

blocks.note: a mustang is a wild horse; its S moves to the front

annotation.surface: A Ford Mustang cruises north along a southern coast road.
annotation.walkthrough: The car named Mustang fits 'driving'; the mustang is the horse, and its S climbs to the top.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the land along the edge of the sea.

entries.clue: Coffee shop rejected American slider — mostly old holidaymakers there? (5,3,3)

indicatorNotes.rejected: something rejected is sent back, so SLEDS turns round
indicatorNotes.mostly: mostly means not quite all, so OLD loses its last letter

blocks.note: Costa is a British coffee shop chain
a sled is the American word for a sledge; in the plural, sent back
OLD without its last letter

annotation.surface: A café turned away an American, and the place is full of elderly tourists.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'old' from the wordplay for its picture: this Spanish coast is famous for older British tourists.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by reputation: the Spanish resort coast crowded with British holidaymakers.

entries.clue: Confusion over cricket officials before international, the second of four (9)

indicatorNotes.the second of: second in order, so the second letter of 'four'

blocks.note: past = over, as in the danger is past
the ICC is the International Cricket Council
I = international
second letter of fOur

annotation.surface: A muddle over umpiring decisions in an international match, with a boundary four in dispute.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over' and 'four' are both cricket words in the surface; neither is used that way here.
annotation.definitionFit: Synonym by extension: a medley or hotchpotch of mixed parts, a jumble.

entries.clue: Work to live, with half going for a raise (4)

indicatorNotes.half going: half of LIVE, the VE, goes away
indicatorNotes.for a raise: what is left of LIVE is raised, which in a down entry turns it upside down

blocks.note: as written

blocks.clueFragment: live, with half going for a raise
blocks.note: LI, half of LIVE, turned upward

annotation.surface: The old grumble that you work to live, then lose half your pay packet chasing a rise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Work to live' is the familiar saying, but only 'Work' is the definition and 'to' goes straight into the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: hard labour.

entries.clue: Contact French city (4)

blocks.note: a noun here, the thing worn on the eye, not the verb
a town in the Pas-de-Calais, in northern France

annotation.surface: An instruction to get in touch with a town in France.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Contact' reads as a verb; it is the noun, short for contact lens.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: a shortening of contact lens, and a town in northern France.

entries.clue: Freedom of movement chimed with European (5)

blocks.note: a bell that chimed rang
E = European

annotation.surface: Free movement, the EU principle, fits in with European thinking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Freedom of movement' reads as the EU principle, which the 'European' strengthens; it means scope to roam.
annotation.definitionFit: Synonym: the scope within which something may move freely.

entries.clue: Dressing area of skin on nail getting black over time (7)

indicatorNotes.getting: the nail skin word gets a B in place of T
indicatorNotes.over: B is put over T, covering and replacing it

blocks.note: the cuticle is the skin at the base of a nail
B = black, as on pencils
T = time, the letter that B replaces

annotation.surface: A bruised nail, the skin round it turning black over time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Area of' reads as part of 'area of skin', but the definition ends at 'area' and 'of' is a link.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a small partitioned booth such as the one you change in at a pool.

entries.clue: Meeting for former students perhaps in complex (9)

blocks.note: OB = old boy, a former pupil; 'perhaps' because old girls count too
a session is a meeting

annotation.surface: A reunion for old students is held in a building complex.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Complex' looks like a group of buildings; it is the psychological sense. An old boys' meeting would be an OB session.
annotation.definitionFit: Synonym from psychology: a fixation that grips the mind, as a complex does.

entries.clue: Drink unusual creation, suitable for all (9)

indicatorNotes.unusual: the letters of CREATION are put in an unusual order

blocks.note: anagram of CREATION
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

annotation.surface: A novel drink mixed so that anyone can enjoy it.
annotation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating meaning suitable for all ages.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a French orange liqueur, one drink among many.

entries.clue: Flat song must cramp tango in star-studded venues (10)

indicatorNotes.must cramp: to cramp is to confine, so PLANE ARIA squeezes T between them

blocks.note: a plane is a flat surface
an aria is a song in an opera
T is tango in the radio alphabet

annotation.surface: A flat, dull song gets in the way of the tango in glitzy clubs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Star-studded' suggests celebrities; these domes are literally studded with projected stars. Flat and song are both music words in the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Witty literal reading: theatres whose domed ceilings are covered in projected stars.

entries.clue: Beg “tonight please”, so desperate for beefy Italian? (9,9)

indicatorNotes.desperate: desperate means frantic, so the letters are thrown about wildly

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 18 letters

annotation.surface: Someone pleading for a meal tonight is starving for a hearty Italian supper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beefy Italian' sounds like a muscular man; it is a dish with a meat sauce.
annotation.definitionFit: Witty description: an Italian dish whose sauce is minced beef.

entries.clue: City joint with pub admits spirited female? (3,5)

indicatorNotes.admits: to admit is to let someone in at the door, so SEAM lets NY inside it

blocks.note: a seam is a joint where pieces meet; split SEA…M
NY = New York
PH = public house on maps

annotation.surface: A city bar lets in a lively woman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spirited' reads as lively; the female here is a nature spirit. The joint is a seam, not a place to drink, though 'pub' is next to it.
annotation.definitionFit: Punning definition: a nymph of the sea is a female spirit, so literally spirited.

entries.clue: Natural in cargo pants (7)

indicatorNotes.pants: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are made a mess of

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: Cargo trousers made from natural fibres.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cargo pants' is one garment in the surface; 'pants' is British slang for rubbish, a sign the letters are poorly arranged.
annotation.definitionFit: Synonym: grown without artificial chemicals, hence natural.

entries.clue: Imminent trial, head of narcs having hidden heroin? (7)

indicatorNotes.having hidden: N sits over the H and hides it, taking its place

blocks.note: a hearing is a trial in court
first letter of narcs
H is slang for heroin; it is replaced

annotation.surface: A drug squad chief is about to face trial, accused of concealing heroin.
annotation.walkthrough: Narcs are American narcotics agents; the surface makes the hidden heroin a crime, but it is the letter replaced.
annotation.definitionFit: Synonym as an adjective: drawing close in time, about to happen.

entries.clue: One developing eggs retracted collecting tube (7)

indicatorNotes.retracted: drawn back, so ROE is read in reverse

blocks.note: roe is fish eggs; reversed to EOR and split E…OR
a duct is a tube

annotation.surface: Something that develops eggs drawing them back through a tube, like a biology lesson.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Developing eggs' reads as one idea; 'One developing' is the definition and 'eggs' starts the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Rare agent noun from educe, to draw out or develop what is latent.

entries.clue: Official line in electronic parts plant (8)

indicatorNotes.parts: to part is to separate, so REF RY moves apart to let IN E into the gap

blocks.note: a ref is a referee, an official
IN as written, E = electronic
RY = railway, a line

annotation.surface: An authorised route through the components of an electronic factory.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parts' looks like components; it is the verb, the official line separating to let the letters in. 'Plant' means an industrial works, not a flower.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: an industrial works for purifying oil or sugar is a kind of plant.

entries.clue: Runaway con largely protected by sword (7)

indicatorNotes.largely: largely means for the most part, so SCAM loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.protected by: EPEE surrounds SCA as a guard

blocks.note: an épée is a fencing sword; split E…PEE
SCAM, a con, without its last letter

annotation.surface: An escaped convict holds most guards at swordpoint.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Con' suggests a convict, which suits a runaway; here it is a swindle.
annotation.definitionFit: Synonym as a noun: someone who has run away, especially from prison.

entries.clue: Heard naughty child immobilise reptile (8)

indicatorNotes.Heard: what is heard is the sound of the word, not its spelling

blocks.note: a naughty child is a little terror; in a non-rhotic British accent it sounds like TERRA
to pin is to hold still

annotation.surface: An unruly child is heard holding down a pet turtle.
annotation.walkthrough: The homophone relies on the British habit of not sounding a final R, so terror and terra match.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a small freshwater turtle, one kind of reptile.

entries.clue: Cut potentially wounding piece? (4-3,7)

blocks.note: the surface wants a sharp edge that may injure; the setter means a barrel cut short
the surface wants a fragment, as of glass; in gangster slang a piece is a gun

annotation.surface: A sharp fragment, perhaps of glass, that could cut and injure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piece' reads as a fragment; in gangster slang a piece is a gun. 'Cut' is the barrel sawn short, and the question mark flags the double reading.
annotation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a gun, or piece, whose barrel has been cut short and which could wound.

entries.clue: Puts a value on presumably female donkeys? (8)

blocks.note: a verb: sets a worth on something
an invented plural, donkey plus the feminine ending found in lioness and actress

annotation.surface: A valuer pricing she-donkeys at a livestock market.
annotation.walkthrough: The second sense is invented, which 'presumably' flags: by analogy with actress and goddess, a female ass would be an ass-ess.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: a plain verb for valuing, and a jokey coinage for she-donkeys.

entries.clue: Boxer swinging both ways in defence (5)

blocks.note: Muhammad Ali, the boxer
slang: someone who swings both ways is bisexual, bi

annotation.surface: A boxer throwing punches left and right to protect himself.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swinging' and 'defence' belong to the ring in the surface; 'swinging both ways' is the idiom for bisexual.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the plea that you were elsewhere is a defence in court.

entries.clue: Had an impact on suffering using ecstasy rather than lithium (8)

indicatorNotes.using: E is put to use in the word
indicatorNotes.rather than: rather than means instead of, so E goes where LI was

blocks.note: afflicted means suffering
E is the drug ecstasy
Li is the chemical symbol for lithium; it is swapped out

annotation.surface: A patient switched from lithium to ecstasy and felt the difference.
annotation.walkthrough: Lithium is a real treatment for mood disorders, which makes the drug swap read as medical history.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the past tense: influenced, made a difference to.

entries.clue: Arrange care for doctor caught in downpour (6)

blocks.note: a verb: to take a child into a family's care without adopting
the doctor of an English nursery rhyme who went to Gloucester in a shower of rain

annotation.surface: A doctor stuck in the rain needs someone to look after him.
annotation.walkthrough: Doctor Foster is from an English nursery rhyme: he went to Gloucester in a shower of rain and stepped in a puddle up to his middle.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: a verb for looking after a child, and a nursery-rhyme doctor.

entries.clue: Wheel attached to single gnarled tree (7,3)

indicatorNotes.gnarled: gnarled means twisted, so SINGLE is twisted into new order
indicatorNotes.attached to: HELM is joined on after the rearranged letters

blocks.note: anagram of SINGLE
the helm is a ship's wheel

annotation.surface: A wheel fixed to a lone, knotted old tree.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gnarled' belongs to the tree in the surface; it is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a large hedgerow species ravaged by Dutch elm disease.

entries.clue: Spotted male animal that’s valued in the States (7)

blocks.note: spotted = saw
a buck is a male deer or rabbit

annotation.surface: A spotted stag, an animal prized in America.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spotted male animal' reads as a fawn-like deer; 'spotted' is the verb. The answer is US slang for a ten-dollar bill.
annotation.definitionFit: Cryptic hint: American slang for a ten-dollar note, a thing with a set value in the States.

entries.clue: Sweet drink after opening of bar, say (12)

indicatorNotes.opening of: a word's opening is its first letter, here the B of 'bar'

blocks.note: first letter of bar
to utter is to say
Scotch whisky

annotation.surface: A sweet drink ordered as soon as the bar opens.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweet drink' reads as one phrase; 'Sweet' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a boiled confection of butter and brown sugar.

entries.clue: Meet to gradually increase backing for broadcast (10)

indicatorNotes.backing: GATHER backs FORE, coming after it
indicatorNotes.broadcast: what is broadcast is heard, so the sound of 'for' is given

blocks.note: fore sounds like 'for'
to gather, as in gather speed, is to increase gradually

annotation.surface: A meeting to build up support for a broadcast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing' reads as support; it tells you GATHER stands behind FORE.
annotation.definitionFit: Synonym: to assemble together.

entries.clue: Cuts of meat to offer cats when duck has gone up (11)

indicatorNotes.when duck has gone up: the O, a duck in cricket, moves up the down entry

blocks.note: to tender is to offer
lions are big cats; the O climbs one place

annotation.surface: Choice meat offered to the cats because the duck flew away.
annotation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O; 'gone up' makes the O move upward in LIONS.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the tenderest cuts from the loin of beef or pork.

entries.clue: Core teacher recalled Pride (6)

indicatorNotes.recalled: called back, so SIR is read backwards

blocks.note: a hub is the core
SIR, a teacher, turned round

annotation.surface: A core-subject teacher is remembered for pride.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Core teacher' reads as a teacher of core subjects; the words split. British pupils call a male teacher sir.
annotation.definitionFit: Synonym: overweening pride, the kind that invites a fall in Greek tragedy.

entries.clue: Small car one advanced across horse country (5,6)

indicatorNotes.across: across means on the far side of, so I A lands beyond ARAB

blocks.note: S = small, plus the car maker Audi
an Arab is a breed of horse
I = one, A = advanced, as in A level

annotation.surface: A tiny car took a step forward across horse country.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Horse country' reads as a phrase for stud farms; 'horse' is wordplay and 'country' alone defines. The Arab breed does come from this region.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a Gulf kingdom, one country among many.

entries.clue: Observe selected element of vow at church (5)

indicatorNotes.selected element of: a selected element is one part taken from a larger whole, here a run of letters

blocks.note: hidden in voW AT CHurch

annotation.surface: Watching a key moment of wedding vows being said in church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Selected element' sounds like choosing one part of the ceremony; it is choosing consecutive letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to look at attentively.

entries.clue: Upset shaved cat enters, hopefully empty, folk’s study (10)

indicatorNotes.Upset: set upside down, so PARED reads upward as DERAP
indicatorNotes.enters: to enter is to go into a place, so MOG goes into the gap in DE…RAP
indicatorNotes.empty: HOPEFULLY loses its inside, leaving HY

blocks.note: PARED, shaved, turned over and split DE…RAP
mog, short for moggy, is British slang for a cat
HopefullY with its middle removed

annotation.surface: A cat, freshly clipped and cross, wanders into a study, hoping it is empty.
annotation.walkthrough: Mog is British slang for a cat. The comma'd 'hopefully empty' reads as the cat's hope, not an instruction to gut the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Paraphrase from the Greek roots: writing about the people, the study of populations.

entries.clue: Fall ill and take off headset, shivering (5,4,5)

indicatorNotes.shivering: shivering letters shake into a new order

blocks.note: to catch on is to become popular, to take off
anagram of HEADSET

annotation.surface: Someone feels unwell, pulls off their headphones and starts shivering.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Take off headset' reads as removing headphones; 'take off' means catch on, and 'shivering' belongs to the wordplay, not the illness.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: a hyperbolic phrase for catching a bad cold.

entries.clue: Being intoxicated, summary of news disheartened son (9)

indicatorNotes.disheartened: the heart, the middle letter L, is removed

blocks.note: HEADLINES, a summary of the news, minus its middle letter L
S = son

annotation.surface: A son, drunk, is dismayed by the news headlines.
annotation.walkthrough: HEADLINES has nine letters, so its heart is the single L in fifth place.
annotation.definitionFit: Paraphrase: the state of being heady, light-headed as with drink.

entries.clue: Vehicle reversing, with endless prejudice gripping old city’s outskirts (8)

indicatorNotes.reversing: a vehicle reversing travels backwards, so BUS is read backwards as SUB
indicatorNotes.gripping: SUB and BIA together grip UR between them

blocks.note: BUS turned round
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia
BIAS, prejudice, without its last letter

annotation.walkthrough: UR is the crossword's favourite old city, the Sumerian Ur. The 's is a link: the old city has outskirts.

entries.clue: Wind energy bound to come up under naysayer (9)

indicatorNotes.under: the reversed piece sits beneath ANTI

annotation.walkthrough: 'Bound to come up' reads as certain to arise; bound is to dart, and 'come up' reverses it.

entries.clue: Woman eating brownie left on piano is managing unaided (4-4)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down entry L sits on top of P

blocks.note: she = a woman; split S…HE
a brownie is a household elf of folklore
L = left
p = piano, quietly

annotation.walkthrough: 'Brownie' is a cake in the surface and a helpful sprite of folklore in the wordplay.

entries.clue: Conjure up pancake, flipped for first lady to consume (7)

indicatorNotes.to consume: to consume is to eat, taking food inside, so EVE takes OCAT inside her

a taco is a folded tortilla, a kind of pancake; flipped to OCAT

entries.clue: Firm upswing controls whip (7)

blocks.note: a surge is an upswing; split S…URGE

annotation.surface: A company's surge in business lets it crack the whip.

entries.clue: At pool, a bikini is regularly left on the counter, which interests psychologist (7)

entries.clue: Poor conductor covering for choir elicited blunders (10)

indicatorNotes.blunders: the letters blunder into a new order

entries.clue: Explicit about writer of nonsense (5)

Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse

annotation.surface: A plain-spoken remark about a writer of nonsense.

entries.clue: Noisily waged battle with cavalier for some days (9)

entries.clue: Northern game — going topless, of course (5)

blocks.note: N = northern
MATCH without its M

annotation.surface: A northern football match where fans go shirtless, naturally.

entries.clue: Lock travel rucksack which has twisted clips (4)

indicatorNotes.twisted: turned round, so the hidden letters read backwards

blocks.note: held in traveL RUCksack, then read backwards

annotation.walkthrough: 'Lock' looks like a padlock for the bag; it is a lock of hair.

entries.clue: Leaders in orthopaedic surgery simply adore bones (4)

indicatorNotes.Leaders in: leaders go at the front, so the leading letter of each following word
